scope: Literature/source review only. No GPU computation, model execution, training, dependency installation, dataset download, or vault calls. Full original arXiv HTML read, including AIST++ appendices; original PDFs retained as source checks. API/repository files inspected as source, not executed.

papers.title: Beat this! Accurate beat tracking without DBN postprocessing
method: 30 s mono input at 22050 Hz; 128-bin mel, 30 Hz-10 kHz, window 1024, hop 441 (=50 Hz), ln(1+1000x). About 20M parameters.

Frontend: convolution stem then 3 blocks of frequency-directed partial transformer, time-directed partial transformer, strided convolution. Frequency is reduced, channels grow; T x 4 x 256 flattens/projected to T x 512.
Main transformer: 6 full-context layers, hidden 512, 16 heads of width 32, rotary position embedding, sigmoid attention gates, FFN 2048. Offline/noncausal, not evidence of online operation.

Two linear heads. Downbeat logits are separate; beat logits=sum(beat-head + downbeat-head logits). This encourages, but does not guarantee, downbeats being beats. Independent binary targets allow beat-only annotated datasets.

Shift-tolerant weighted BCE: positive-class weight=negative/positive count; max pool predictions over 7 frames; ignore negative loss within 6 frames of a positive label (13-frame max pool on labels). The nominal +/-3-frame training allowance must not be interpreted as precise annotations.

Minimal postprocessor: local maximum over +/-3 frames, probability>0.5; plateau center; snap downbeats to nearest predicted beat. No DBN tempo/meter assumptions. Paper says nonoverlapping 30 s excerpts; current release instead pads/discards 6 border frames and overlaps chunks (record source version).
Augmentations: pitch -5..+6 semitones; tempo +/-4/8/12/16/20 percent, precomputed but not combined; 0-6 masks of 0.5-2 s using locally shuffled partitions rather than zero masking.

Training: 100 epochs, AdamW, max LR 0.0008 after 1000-step warmup, cosine decay, weight decay 0.01, effective batch 64 via 8x8 accumulation. Sample multiple 30-s excerpts per longer song. Select/report F1 rather than treating rising validation BCE as automatic failure.
data_and_labels: 4556 train/validation tracks over 18 dataset groupings; 993 GTZAN test tracks after annotation exclusions. Eight-fold cross-validation for Table 1; new approximately 15% per-dataset validation split for ablations.

Training datasets: Simac, SMC, Hainsworth, Ballroom, HJDB, Beatles, Harmonix, RWC classical/pop/royalty-free/jazz, TapCorrect, JAAH, Filosax backing tracks, ASAP excluding rubato-annotated tracks, Groove MIDI tracks >20s, GuitarSet comping (not solos), Candombe.

Beat/downbeat annotations can be imprecise, inconsistent or ambiguous; some passages do not support a unique beat. F1 evaluation uses mir_eval defaults, +/-70 ms matching, first 5 s discarded. CMLt/AMLt add continuity; AMLt also permits alternate metric levels. Output grid is 20 ms, not label accuracy.

Annotations v1.0 are required for exact published reproduction. Annotation repo warns some RWC conversions were incorrect and preserved for reproducibility; a corrected version changes the target definition.

papers.title: All-In-One Metrical And Functional Structure Analysis With Neighborhood Attentions on Demixed Audio
read_sections: 3 Experiments (3.1-3.3, Table1); original-PDF Figure3 labels/ablation values also read
method: Joint shared representation with beat, downbeat, segment-boundary and functional-label heads. Tempo in the released API is postprocessed from beat intervals, not a fifth learned tempo head.

Hybrid Transformer Demucs produces 4 sources (bass, drums, other, vocals). Convolution/max-pool frontend feeds 11 transformer modules with C=24. About 300K task-network parameters, excluding the pretrained separator.

Each module pairs temporal 1-D dilated neighborhood attention and local 2-D instrumental/time neighborhood attention. Two temporal branches have dilation d and 2d; exponential depth schedule to 2^10 and 2^11. Paper reports approximately 41/82 s receptive fields for those branches, not a streaming latency guarantee.
Nearest-available-neighbor windows avoid large time-axis zero padding near boundaries. Actual 5x5 instrument attention still pads the instrument axis because NATTEN lacks nonsquare kernels.

Beat/downbeat outputs use DBN postprocessing; segment boundaries use sliding-average normalization/peak picking with 24-s window, without the earlier work's threshold step. Current metrical source uses a joint DBN constrained to 3/4 and 4/4.

Current source details beyond paper prose: 44100 Hz, 2048 window, 441 hop (=100 Hz), 81 log-frequency bins, 30-17000 Hz. Independent linear heads over concatenated stem embeddings: three BCE event heads, one 10-class cross-entropy function head. Default task weights beat/downbeat/section/function=1/3/15/0.1; losses use frame masks.

Current training code quantizes event times with librosa.time_to_frames; beat/downbeat labels widen +/-1 frame with 0.5 shoulders; section labels widen +/-2 frames with decaying shoulders. This is source behavior, not evidence labels are accurate to 10-20 ms.

Paper training: PyTorch 2.0, NATTEN, madmom, RAdam lr .005; SWA lr .15; plateau lr factor .3, weight decay .00025; batch 1, songs >5 min randomly cropped to 5 min, early stop after 30 unimproved epochs. No data augmentation or extra supervised datasets.
data_and_labels: Only Harmonix Set used for supervised tasks; cleaned audio/annotation versions and merged functional labels according to Wang et al. 2022. Eight folds: 6 train, 1 validation, 1 test.

Beat/downbeat F1 matches within +/-70 ms; CMLt and AMLt measure continuity. Segment HR.5F uses +/-0.5 s. Functional labeling uses pairwise frame clustering F1 (PWF) and normalized entropy F1 (Sf), not ordinary 10-class accuracy.

Release functional labels: start, end, intro, outro, break, bridge, inst, solo, verse, chorus. These are section functions, not labeled drops, lighting accents, fixture programs, or calibrated event salience.
README warns different MP3 decoders can shift timing by roughly 20-40 ms; recommends canonical WAV via ffmpeg for all processing. This is an implementation warning, not a published timing benchmark.

published_comparisons.caveat: Different task removals: removing labels slightly improves downbeats but harms segmentation; removing BOTH rhythm heads improves label PWF but slightly harms segmentation. Not proof all heads mutually improve.

limitations: Ablation shows beat/downbeat/segmentation can benefit each other, but not uniform positive transfer: removing the functional-label head raises downbeat F1 slightly; removing BOTH beat and downbeat heads raises functional-label PWF. This does not isolate downbeat-only interference with labeling.

Evidence is Western-pop Harmonix cross-validation; genre/OOD generalization is not established. Longer contexts particularly help section tasks; one short beat window is not sufficient evidence for sections.
Model parameter count excludes Demucs. NATTEN, Demucs, madmom and full-song processing create dependency/runtime costs absent from the 300K headline.
DBN metrical constraints can fail for changing/odd meter and strong tempo changes. Four task probabilities are not validated light controls. No causal streaming claim.

papers.title: AI Choreographer: Music Conditioned 3D Dance Generation with AIST++
read_sections: Appendix A Dataset Details (Table 5, reconstruction, validation)
method: FACT is a motion generator, not a beat tracker. Takes 120-frame/2-s seed motion and 240-frame/4-s audio features aligned at first frame. Full attention, two modality encoders, early concatenation, 12-layer cross-modal transformer.

Main configuration: 2 audio and 2 motion layers, 12 cross-modal layers; 800 hidden channels, 10 heads. Train on future 20 motion frames with L2 loss; autoregressive inference retains only the first new predicted frame per step at 60 Hz.

Audio representation=35 dimensions: onset envelope, 20 MFCC, 12 chroma, one-hot onset peaks and one-hot librosa beat estimates. Motion representation=219 dimensions (24x9 rotation matrices + xyz global translation). Learned positional encoding in modality encoders.

Full-attention plus multi-frame supervision improves long-rollout stability versus causal shift-by-1 and full-attention future-1 variants; early/deep cross-modal fusion reduces music ignoring versus late fusion. These results are about motion generation, not direct audio timing supervision.
Adam batch16; learning rate 1e-4 ->1e-5 at60k ->1e-6 at100k; 300k total steps, reported 3 days/4 TPUs. No replication or training done in this review.

Official preprocessing uses SR=60x512=30720, hop512, librosa beat_track(start_bpm parsed from AIST audio filename, tightness=100). This uses dataset BPM knowledge in feature construction and does not supply independent human beat ground truth.
data_and_labels: 1408 motion sequences, 5.2 h (18694.6 s), 60 songs, 30 dancers, 10 genres, nine camera views. Original AIST camera views are not 9 independent dances; the 10.1M images versus ~1.1M motion frames differ by view multiplicity.

Per frame: 17 COCO joints in 2D/3D and 24 SMPL rotations plus scale/translation. Reconstructed from 2D detections, bundle adjustment, triangulation with temporal/bone constraints, SMPL fitting; no measured 3D mocap truth.

Basic instructional choreography is repeated across all six songs/tempi in a genre; about 85% basic and 15% advanced. Paper separates both song and choreography: 40 test choreographies from ten songs and 329 training choreographies. Clip-level random splits leak repeated motions/music.

Annotation time grid is exact 60 FPS even when raw videos have slightly different FPS. Dataset download page requires conversion to exact60; inspect actual timestamps and alignment, not raw nominal FPS. Recommended ignore_list excludes poor reconstructions.

BeatAlign music reference=librosa-estimated beats, kinematic events=local minima of kinetic velocity. Score=mean over kinetic events exp(-nearest_audio_distance_in_frames^2/(2*3^2)) at60 FPS. sigma3 frames=50 ms Gaussian scale, not hard tolerance, not label precision.

BeatAlign is deliberately one-way because not every audio beat need be expressed in dance. It does not check recall/coverage of audio beats or distinguish correct downbeat/bar level. It is not ground-truth lighting accent alignment.

published_comparisons.comparator: Dancenet (Zhuang et al., Music2Dance) trained on the same split
published_comparisons.caveat: FID uses handcrafted kinetic/geometric motion features, not lighting or an Inception image model.
The paper calls these lower/upper bounds; they are empirical comparators, not mathematical floor/ceiling, and use model-estimated audio beats.

published_comparisons.source: Table2, Sec5.2.4, AppendixB; 30 participants per baseline, 10 side-by-side 10s videos each, randomized left/right
published_comparisons.caveat: Despite FACT BeatAlign0.241 versus random0.213, users preferred real unpaired motion. Authors attribute this to expressiveness bias; the direct evidence is metric/user preference divergence, not proof the users were wrong.

limitations: No physical dancer-floor model; foot sliding/floating remains. Deterministic given seed/audio, although different seeds permit diversity. Not a lighting system.

Dataset reconstruction validates consistency with detected 2D joints, not actual 3D truth or beat truth. Main text PCKh98.7% differs from Appendix98.4%; do not quote either as verified mocap accuracy.

Repeated instructional choreography and genre/song pairing make correlation confounding possible. The paper's splits do not by themselves establish within-genre audio-specific learning for a new LightSem descriptor task.

BeatAlign can disagree with human motion-music preference. Velocity minima depend on reconstruction/filtering/movement type; static/frozen or dense-event pathologies need explicit controls in any reuse.

The official scores.py read here computes motion FIDs; it does not contain a BeatAlign implementation. Do not claim code-verified reproduction of the paper's BeatAlign extraction details beyond its equation/text.

campaign_implications.lighting_policy_not_beat_tracker: A beat/downbeat tracker estimates a latent musical clock; it does not decide which events merit lighting accents. A lighting policy chooses a subset/metrical level, suppression and silence, attack/hold/decay, anticipation or syncopation, intensity and spatial/color action. Neither beat labels nor dance velocity minima are lighting-accent targets. Evaluate the timing instrument separately from the emitted light policy; musical F1 cannot establish lighting quality.
campaign_implications.approved_architecture_scope: Use direct audio rhythm for LIGHT timing; internal motion may supply spatial style. These papers do not justify retiming or retraining a dancer to satisfy a lighting request.
campaign_implications.label_precision: Keep sample rate, detector-output grid, human annotation uncertainty, evaluation tolerance, and rendered/DMX update interval distinct. 50/100 Hz model output is not evidence for 20/10 ms human beat labels. Section boundary labels are coarser still. Do not optimize a sample-accurate loss against uncertain marks without an uncertainty model.
campaign_implications.conditioning_design: Beat This suggests shared audio features, distinct sparse beat/downbeat heads, soft hierarchical consistency, imbalance-aware shift-tolerant losses. All-In-One supports beat/downbeat/segment multi-task coupling, not a claim that every added task helps: functional labels and downbeats can compete. Treat transfer to lighting as a hypothesis, not a published result.
campaign_implications.calibration: Beat This deliberately learns overconfident peaks. Its sigmoid magnitude is not a validated confidence/abstention estimate. Calibrate confidence on independent annotations before using it as a safety or fallback gate.
campaign_implications.timing_measurements: Report beat/downbeat F1 together with named comparator, continuity, signed timing residuals and tempo/meter failures. F1 at 70 ms can hide fine timing offsets. Standardize source PCM, time origins, trim and resampling; report rendered-light timing separately with density- and brightness-matched controls.
campaign_implications.heldout_protocol: Prefer external, rights-cleared songs with expert beat/downbeat marks and adjudicated ambiguity, frozen before model selection. Hash exact audio, record sample offsets and annotation provenance. Audit exact recordings, compositions/arrangements, artists and training dataset IDs as relevant. For existing corpora use matched out-of-fold checkpoints and original split manifests, never all-fold ensembles. Mark unresolved overlap as descriptive evaluation only.
campaign_implications.no_pose_ground_truth: AIST++ kinetic-velocity minima are a motion-derived proxy, not ground-truth audio beats. Position/pose minima are not even the same proxy. Reconstruction noise, smoothing, freezing, feet versus torso motion, and beat-doubling can change the proxy without improved musical perception. BeatAlign rewards one-way proximity, not coverage, correct bar position, light output, or aesthetic acceptance.
campaign_implications.metric_scope: AIST++ authors call real-paired and random-paired scores an upper/lower calibration; neither is a mathematical ceiling/floor or a null calibrated to the LightSem cohort. Use cohort-specific metronome and shift/null controls, and do not transfer their absolute scores across feature definitions or corpora.
